source.read_scope: Assumption 2.7; complete Lemma 2.9 and proof, Remark 2.10, Lemma 2.11 and proof, printed pp. 6–7; complete Theorem 10.2 proof pp. 53–55 previously read in this session, with the conjugation and factorization paragraphs pp. 54–55 reread for this focused check.

conclusions: Lemma 2.9 identifies A12 with A23 and A21 with A32, and proves T(A12 A21)=T(A23 A32). It identifies the two adjacent product ideals, rather than constructing an independent second adjacent factor.
Remark 2.10 transports multiplication by that same ideal through three module identities. It does not replace the ideal by its square or provide a product of independent congruence ideals.
In the definition I=T(A12 A21+A13 A31+A23 A32), the equal adjacent ideals occur by ideal sum; J+J=J. There is no multiplicity-two length contribution from that repetition.

Theorem 10.2 uses complex conjugation to identify the two adjacent Greenberg Selmer groups, and its congruence quotient (10.6) contains one adjacent and one long-root L-factor. No extra adjacent congruence length follows from this isomorphism.

For the formal parallel specialization Psi=chi^(e+1), Psi^(-c)chi=Psi^(-1)chi already as characters. The cited conjugation isomorphism alone gives no independently controlled additional factor for the d=2 conormal estimate.
limits: This is a check of these exact symmetry and conjugation clauses, not a proof that every possible strengthened comparison is impossible.
No claim that the actual source local conditions meet the hypotheses of BK2026; those separate mismatches remain.
No new Selmer or class-group vanishing, no arithmetic gate movement.
